item.title: From the editors: Our apology and vow to develop more extensive editorial policies around covering protests
item.description: In our Feb. 5 issue, The Ithacan wrongly identified a protester in the photo caption. When we wrongly identified this person, we failed to meet our mission to thoughtfully report for our community's best interests, and our commitment to minimize harm. We are deeply sorry for this error and will use this as an opportunity to reflect on our editorial practices and processes. item.title: Editorial: Bad Bunny and the Big Game – The influential power of art and sports
item.description: It is hard to say that the NFL was entirely making a political statement by choosing Bad Bunny for the halftime show. It equally and realistically could have been functioning as a business, strategically attempting to grow viewership as well as increase publicity. But what is clear is the impact and influential power the NFL, as well as sports in general, has on culture as well as politics in the United States. item.title: 2026 Super Bowl ads: campaigns that scored and fumbled on game day
item.description: The Super Bowl has the largest viewership of any televised event in the United States, with over 127 million people tuning in for the 2025 Super Bowl. However, not every viewer crowding around a coffee table of chips and boneless wings is watching for the big game. Advertising spots are precious for companies trying to reach the widest audience possible, leading to advertising campaigns going above and beyond to make their ad worth the price tag on the ad spot.
